comments.body: 2026-10-05: not reproduced against Claude Code 2.1.290. Both paths send the same daemon Send event (and did at 0.12.0). /clear ran as a command pasted with its Return, pasted with a Return 2 s later, typed as keys, pasted mid-turn, and through the daemon with no window. Evidence: corpus/claude-code-2.1.290/clear.txt, docs/observations/claude-code-2.1.290.md.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
With no window running, the daemon's `pane send` delivers a slash command to Claude Code as a chat message rather than as the command, while the same two sends through the window run it. `--confirm` reports success either way. ## Measured: muster 0.12.0, 2026-09-30 An agent in a dev-box pane gave two worker agents (Claude Code, in panes beside it) a fresh context before their next assignment, the way the parallel-work flow says to: muster pane send --pane

"/clear" --confirm && muster pane send --pane

"" --enter - With the window attached, the first worker's context was cleared: its title reset and its context meter dropped. - Minutes later the window had quit, and the daemon answered the same two sends for the second worker (`nothing is listening on ~/.muster/daemon/window-release-.sock ... pane send ... still work, answered by this machine's muster-daemon`). Both exited 0. The worker's next turn was a user message whose whole text was `/clear`; nothing was cleared, and the worker spent the turn investigating the odd message and reported "your /clear reached me as a chat message, not as the command". **Known and not known.** The two outcomes are measured, from the workers' own reports and the pane's context meter. That the daemon path delivers the text as a bracketed paste, which Claude Code takes as text rather than a command, is inference: nothing here has checked the bytes either path writes. ## Why it matters `/clear` and `/compact` sent from one agent to another are how an orchestrating agent manages a worker's context, and they only work as prompts. A send that turns them into chat costs the worker a turn and leaves its context as it was, and `--confirm` says it worked. It also means the daemon fallback is not a like-for-like substitute for the window, which is what its message promises. ## Things that might be true - **Make the daemon's send write what the window's does**, so the receiving harness cannot tell them apart. - **Type a leading slash command as keys, not as a paste**, on both paths. - **Have `--confirm` tell a slash command taken as a command from one taken as text**, or say in the fallback message and in `muster docs limits` that slash commands need the window. Related: a_2I7Acusq4 (done) is the paste placeholder that swallowed a Return; this is the case where the Return did submit, but as the wrong thing.
title: 💬 pane send without a window delivers a slash command as chat
